maml:description.maml:para: Finds access control entries in Active Directory that grant rights to principals that no longer exist.

Walks every object under one or more search bases, reads each security descriptor, resolves every identity reference, and reports the ones that cannot be resolved. Nothing is changed.
Each orphaned access control entry is written to the pipeline as an OrphanedSIDResult with the object's distinguished name, the unresolvable SID, the rights it still grants, and an analysis of where the SID probably came from. The same rows are written to -OutputPath as CSV when that parameter is given. A summary (objects processed, orphaned SIDs found, unverified SIDs, duration, peak memory) goes to the console and the log.
A SID is reported orphaned only when every directory lookup completed and none found it. When no lookup found the SID but at least one failed for another reason, such as a timeout, access denied or an unreachable domain controller, the SID may still belong to a live principal. It is listed with VerificationStatus Unverified, Confidence Low and a VerificationError that names each failed lookup, so it can be re-checked. Remove-OrphanedSid never removes an unverified SID. Unverified results are not cached, so a later object or a later run looks the SID up again.
A SID from a trusted domain can only be checked by that domain. When its domain controllers answer that the principal is gone, the SID is reported orphaned with LikelySource Foreign Domain/Trust; review those rows before a removal, since the owner sits outside the domain being cleaned. When they cannot be reached or the trust is broken, the SID is reported Unverified, and each such lookup waits for the trust to time out (about 40 seconds per SID in testing).
An account that cannot read a principal gets no error from Active Directory, only an empty search, so missing read permission alone does not make a SID unverified. Run the command as an account that can read every object in scope.
Results stream to batch files in the temp directory while the run is in progress; the files are removed when the command finishes unless -PreserveTempFiles is set.
JSON configuration file. Only WellKnownSIDPatterns, ProtectedSIDs, BatchSize, MemoryCheckInterval, EnableDetailedLogging, LogLevel, LogFilePath, EnableLogFileRotation and MaxLogFileSizeMB are read.
Identifier carried through every log line and result row. Generated when omitted.
Also report access control entries inherited from parent containers. More rows and a longer run; by default only explicit entries are reported.
Lowest level written to the log file. Security events are written at every level.
Log file. Defaults to .\Logs\Find-OrphanedSid_<yyyyMMdd_HHmmss>.log under the current directory.
Working-set threshold in megabytes at which garbage collection is forced. Default 1024.
Retry attempts for a transient Active Directory failure on one object. Default 3.
CSV file to write the results to, in addition to the pipeline. The parent folder must exist.
Keep the streaming batch files under $env:TEMP\OrphanedSid-<CorrelationId>\ for inspection after the run.
Distinguished name of one or more containers to search. Accepts pipeline input. Defaults to the current domain root when omitted.
Write progress and the summary to the log file only.
Distinguished names, by value or by the `DistinguishedName` property of a piped object such as the output of `Get-ADOrganizationalUnit` or `Get-ADObject`.

One object per orphaned access control entry, with `ObjectDN`, `ObjectClass`, `OrphanedSID`, `LikelySource`, `Confidence`, `AnalysisNotes`, `AccessControlType`, `ActiveDirectoryRights`, `InheritanceType`, `ObjectType`, `InheritedObjectType`, `IsInherited`, `ProcessingMethod`, `ActionTaken`, `VerificationStatus`, `VerificationError`, `CorrelationId` and `Timestamp`.
`VerificationStatus` is `Orphaned` when every lookup completed and none found the SID, and `Unverified` when a lookup failed; `VerificationError` then names each failed lookup.

maml:introduction.maml:para: Find-OrphanedSid -SearchBase 'OU=Users,DC=contoso,DC=com'
DESCRIPTION: Lists every orphaned ACE under the Users OU OUTPUT: One OrphanedSIDResult per orphaned access control entry USE CASE: A first look at how much cleanup an OU needs
Find-OrphanedSid -SearchBase 'DC=contoso,DC=com' -IncludeInherited -OutputPath '.\Reports\audit.csv'
DESCRIPTION: Audits the whole domain including inherited entries and keeps a CSV OUTPUT: Result objects on the pipeline and the same rows in audit.csv USE CASE: Periodic compliance evidence
Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter * -SearchScope OneLevel | Find-OrphanedSid | Group-Object OrphanedSID | Sort-Object Count -Descending
DESCRIPTION: Pipes OUs in and groups the findings by SID OUTPUT: The SIDs that appear most often across the domain USE CASE: Deciding which deleted principals left the widest footprint
$results = Find-OrphanedSid -SearchBase 'OU=Servers,DC=contoso,DC=com' $results | Where-Object VerificationStatus -eq 'Unverified' | Select-Object ObjectDN, OrphanedSID, VerificationError

DESCRIPTION: Lists the SIDs a failed directory lookup left unverified, with the reason OUTPUT: One row per unverified entry, naming each lookup that failed USE CASE: Re-checking after a domain controller outage or a permissions problem before cleanup

maml:description.maml:para: Removes orphaned access control entries from Active Directory objects after backing up each ACL.

Runs the same discovery as Find-OrphanedSid and then, for every object that carries an orphaned entry, validates each SID against the protected and well-known SID lists, writes a Clixml backup of the object's ACL, and removes the orphaned entries. The backup for a run lands in a timestamped folder so a whole run can be undone with Restore-OrphanedSidBackup.
Only SIDs that every directory lookup confirmed missing are removed. When a lookup fails for a reason other than "not found", such as a timeout, access denied or an unreachable domain controller, the SID may still belong to a live principal: it is marked Unverified, left in place, and named in a warning together with the lookup that failed. The summary reports how many SIDs were unverified. Re-run once the domain controller is reachable and the account can read the targets.
A SID from a trusted domain is removed only when that domain answers that the principal no longer exists; an unreachable trusted domain leaves the SID unverified and in place. Run Find-OrphanedSid or -WhatIf first and review entries with LikelySource Foreign Domain/Trust: their owners sit outside the domain being cleaned.
The command has ConfirmImpact High: it asks once before changing anything. -WhatIf previews the run, listing the entries that would be removed, and creates no backup. An unattended run (scheduled task, CI) cannot answer the prompt and must pass -Force or -Confirm:$false.
Each removal is written to the pipeline as a RemovalOperationResult; -OutputPath writes the discovered entries as CSV.
Folder that receives the per-run backup subfolder. Defaults to .\Backup under the current directory. The parent folder must exist; the backup folder itself is created.
JSON configuration file; see Find-OrphanedSid for the keys read. ProtectedSIDs and WellKnownSIDPatterns are the ones that matter here.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
Identifier carried through every log line, backup file and result. Generated when omitted.
Proceed without the confirmation prompt. Required for unattended runs. -WhatIf still wins.

Also evaluate inherited access control entries. Inherited entries cannot be removed from the child object, so they are not touched there: each is named in a Warning, `Not removing inherited entry for orphaned SID <SID> on <DN>: it is inherited from a parent object, so remove it there`, and the object is neither backed up nor changed for it. The explicit entry is removed on the parent when the parent is in the search base.
Lowest level written to the log file. Security events are written at every level.
Log file. Defaults to .\Logs\Remove-OrphanedSid_<yyyyMMdd_HHmmss>.log.
Working-set threshold in megabytes at which garbage collection is forced. Default 1024.
Retry attempts for a transient Active Directory failure on one object. Default 3.
CSV file for the discovered entries. The parent folder must exist.
Keep the streaming batch files after the run.
Distinguished name of one or more containers to clean. Accepts pipeline input. Defaults to the current domain root when omitted.
Write progress and the summary to the log file only.
Runs the command in a mode that only reports what would happen without performing the actions.
Distinguished names, by value or by the `DistinguishedName` property of a piped object such as the output of `Get-ADOrganizationalUnit` or `Get-ADObject`.

One object per object changed, covering all of its orphaned entries, with `ObjectDN`, `IntendedRemovals`, `ActualRemovals`, `FailedRemovals`, `RemovedSIDs`, `FailedSIDs`, `BlockedSIDs`, `Success`, `ErrorMessage`, `ProcessingTime`, `CorrelationId` and `SecurityValidation`.

maml:introduction.maml:para: Remove-OrphanedSid -SearchBase 'OU=Decommissioned,DC=contoso,DC=com' -WhatIf
DESCRIPTION: Shows what would be removed without touching anything OUTPUT: A WhatIf line for the run and one per object with entries that would be removed USE CASE: The review step before a cleanup
Remove-OrphanedSid -SearchBase 'OU=Decommissioned,DC=contoso,DC=com' -BackupPath 'D:\ADBackups'

DESCRIPTION: Prompts once, backs up every affected ACL to D:\ADBackups\<timestamp>\, then removes OUTPUT: One RemovalOperationResult per object changed USE CASE: An interactive cleanup with the backup on a dedicated drive
Remove-OrphanedSid -SearchBase 'OU=Servers,DC=contoso,DC=com' -Force -CorrelationId 'CHG0012345' -OutputPath '.\Reports\CHG0012345.csv'
DESCRIPTION: Unattended removal tagged with a change number OUTPUT: Result objects, a CSV, a log and a backup folder that all carry CHG0012345 USE CASE: A scheduled task or a pipeline step

maml:description.maml:para: Restores Active Directory ACLs from a backup folder written by Remove-OrphanedSid.

Reads the Clixml backup files in -BackupPath, validates each one (format, object DN, SDDL and its SHA256 hash), applies the saved security descriptor to the object, and reads the ACL back to verify the result.
-TargetObjectDN decides the scope. A container (an OU or the domain root) restores every object that is the container or sits under it. A single object restores only backups whose recorded object DN equals -TargetObjectDN, compared without regard to letter case. Either way each object is restored once, from its most recent backup in the folder. -BackupPath is the folder that holds the .xml files, normally one timestamped run folder under the Remove-OrphanedSid backup root.
The command has ConfirmImpact High: it asks once before writing anything. -WhatIf previews the restore. An unattended run must pass -Force or -Confirm:$false.
One result object per target is written to the pipeline; -OutputPath writes the same rows as CSV.
Folder containing the backup .xml files. Must exist.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
Identifier carried through every log line and result. Generated when omitted.
Proceed without the confirmation prompt. Required for unattended runs.
Lowest level written to the log file. Security events are written at every level.
Log file. Defaults to .\Logs\Restore-OrphanedSidBackup_<yyyyMMdd_HHmmss>.log.
CSV file for the restore results. The parent folder must exist.
Write progress and the summary to the log file only.
Distinguished name of the object or container to restore. Accepts pipeline input.
Runs the command in a mode that only reports what would happen without performing the actions.
Distinguished names, by value or by the `DistinguishedName` property of a piped object such as the output of `Get-ADOrganizationalUnit` or `Get-ADObject`.

One object per target. For a container it summarises the run (`TotalObjects`, `SuccessfulRestores`, `FailedRestores`, `IndividualResults`); for a single object it is that object's restore result. Both carry `Success`, `TargetObjectDN`, `EntriesRestored`, `ErrorMessage` and `CorrelationId`.

maml:introduction.maml:para: Restore-OrphanedSidBackup -TargetObjectDN 'CN=SRV01,OU=Servers,DC=contoso,DC=com' -BackupPath '.\Backup\20260703_104232' -WhatIf
DESCRIPTION: Previews restoring SRV01 from one run folder without changing it OUTPUT: WhatIf lines naming the backup folder and the object USE CASE: Confirming the right run folder before a rollback
Restore-OrphanedSidBackup -TargetObjectDN 'OU=Servers,DC=contoso,DC=com' -BackupPath 'D:\ADBackups\20260703_104232' -Force

DESCRIPTION: Rolls back every object under the Servers OU from one run's backups, unattended OUTPUT: One summary result for the OU, with each object's result in IndividualResults USE CASE: Undoing a cleanup that removed an entry still in use
Import-Csv .\Reports\CHG0012345.csv | Select-Object -ExpandProperty ObjectDN -Unique | Restore-OrphanedSidBackup -BackupPath 'D:\ADBackups\20260703_104232' -Force
DESCRIPTION: Restores exactly the objects a removal run reported OUTPUT: One result per object USE CASE: Targeted rollback driven by the removal's own CSV
